text: It is crucial to recognise. <break time="0.8s" /> The potential ethical considerations arising from using AI in market research. <break time="0.8s" /> For example. <break time="0.8s" /> Given that researchers use historical data. <break time="0.8s" /> To train the optimising process of AI algorithms. <break time="0.8s" /> There is a risk. <break time="0.8s" /> That the algorithm may reinforce biased traits and or discriminatory performances. <break time="0.8s" /> Another underlying concern arises. <break time="0.8s" /> Through how data is collected and analysed. <break time="0.8s" /> On the Internet and social media. <break time="0.8s" /> In some cases. <break time="0.8s" /> It is not evident. <break time="0.8s" /> That the purpose of a website or an online game. <break time="0.8s" /> Is to capture leads. <break time="0.8s" /> And, in other cases. <break time="0.8s" /> Parts of social media conversations are taken. <break time="0.8s" /> Without asking permission from the interlocutors. <break time="0.8s" /> All of which may raise privacy concerns. <break time="0.8s" /> And or violations of data protection laws. <break time="0.8s" /> To reduce these risks. <break time="0.8s" /> Companies must prioritise ethical considerations. <break time="0.8s" /> And ensure transparency and accountability. <break time="0.8s" /> In using AI. <break time="0.8s" /> It includes. <break time="0.8s" /> Regular evaluations of AI models. <break time="0.8s" /> For potential bias or discrimination behaviour. <break time="0.8s" /> Being transparent with customers. <break time="0.8s" /> About how data is collected and used. <break time="0.8s" /> And allowing customers. <break time="0.8s" /> To freely opt in or opt out of information provision.
